title: VPN Bandwidth Consumption
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'VPN Bandwidth Consumption' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_vpn_bandwidth_consumption` (UC-17.2.7), SOC dashboard panel "Network — VPN Bandwidth Consumption", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=vpn` sourcetype='cisco:asa' that satisfy the UC-17.2.7 SPL filters for 'VPN Bandwidth Consumption'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `vpn` / `cisco:asa` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.2.7.

dataSources: VPN session accounting (bytes in/out) Collected via Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: `Splunk_TA_cisco-asa`, `Splunk_TA_paloalto` (GlobalProtect), `TA-fortinet_fortigate`, `Splunk_TA_juniper`, RADIUS accounting — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)
spl:
index=vpn sourcetype="cisco:asa"
| stats sum(bytes_in) as bytes_in, sum(bytes_out) as bytes_out by user
| eval total_gb=round((bytes_in+bytes_out)/1073741824,2)
| sort -total_gb
| head 20
description: Per-user bandwidth tracking identifies heavy users, guides capacity planning, and detects potential data exfiltration.
value: Security and network teams identify users consuming disproportionate VPN bandwidth, catching potential data exfiltration through abnormal upload ratios and supporting capacity planning for remote work infrastructure.
implementation: Track VPN session byte counters per user. Alert on users with excessive upload (potential data exfiltration). Report on bandwidth distribution for capacity planning. Identify optimization opportunities (video offload, split-tunnel).
visualization: Bar chart (bandwidth by user), Pie chart (upload vs download), Line chart (total bandwidth trend), Table (top bandwidth consumers).

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Remote workforce login storm** — Morning VPN/ZTNA session spike for 'VPN Bandwidth Consumption'. Compare with historical same-hour baseline.

2. **IdP or SAML metadata refresh** — Brief auth failures during federation cert rotation.

3. **Split-tunnel policy change** — New route advertisements shift traffic patterns.

4. **Synthetic ZTNA health checks** — Monitoring probes from known appliance IPs.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `user`, `src`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Add-on for Cisco ASA (`sourcetype=cisco:asa`). Data in `index=vpn`.
• Key fields: `user`, `bytes_in`, `bytes_out`, `action=session_disconnect` (ASA reports cumulative bytes at disconnect).
• For real-time bandwidth (not just session totals): configure NetFlow from the VPN interface and use `sourcetype=cisco:ios:netflow` or SNMP polling.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Verify byte counters:
```spl
index=vpn sourcetype="cisco:asa" action="session_disconnect" earliest=-24h
| where isnotnull(bytes_in) AND bytes_in>0
| stats sum(bytes_in) as total_in sum(bytes_out) as total_out by user
| eval total_gb=round((total_in+total_out)/1073741824, 2)
| sort - total_gb
| head 10
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — Bandwidth by user:
```spl
index=vpn sourcetype="cisco:asa" action="session_disconnect" earliest=-24h
| stats sum(bytes_in) as in_b sum(bytes_out) as out_b count as sessions by user
| eval total_gb=round((in_b+out_b)/1073741824, 2)
| eval upload_gb=round(out_b/1073741824, 2)
| eval upload_pct=round(out_b/(in_b+out_b)*100, 1)
| where total_gb > 1
| sort - total_gb
```

Understanding this SPL: Ranks users by VPN bandwidth consumption. The `upload_pct` is critical — normal VPN usage (web browsing, email) is 80-90% download. A user with >40% upload may be transferring large files outbound, which could indicate data exfiltration, backup operations, or legitimate large file transfers (video production, CAD files). The threshold of 1 GB filters out routine users.

Step 3 — Validate
(a) On ASA: `show vpn-sessiondb detail | grep bytes` for active sessions.
(b) Compare top users with network monitoring tools (NetFlow, SNMP).

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard: Row 1 — "Total VPN bandwidth (GB, 24h)", "Top consumer". Row 2 — Bar chart: top 20 users. Row 3 — Timechart: aggregate bandwidth over 7 days.
Alert: Trigger when any user exceeds 10 GB upload in 24h.

Runbook:
1. **Large upload** — Correlate with DLP data. May be legitimate (cloud backup) or exfiltration.
2. **Overall bandwidth trending up** — More remote users or changed work patterns. Plan capacity.
3. **Single user dominating** — May be running automated tools or streaming. Investigate.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **`bytes_in`/`bytes_out` always zero** — Some ASA versions only report bytes in specific log messages. Check message IDs 722023, 113019.
• **Bytes only at disconnect** — This is normal for ASA. For real-time monitoring, use NetFlow/SNMP.
grandmaExplanation: We track how much data each person sends and receives through our remote connection, and if someone is uploading an unusually large amount, we check to make sure they are not moving company data somewhere they should not.
hardware: Cisco ASA 5506-X/5508-X/5516-X/5525-X/5545-X/5555-X, ASAv, Cisco Secure Firewall 3100/4200; Palo Alto PA-220/PA-440/PA-3200/PA-5200, GlobalProtect; Fortinet FortiGate 60F/100F/200F/600F/1800F, FortiGate SSL-VPN; Juniper SRX300/SRX1500/SRX4100/SRX4200, Junos Dynamic VPN
